summary: In Greek mythology, Aethalides (Ancient Greek Αἰθαλίδης) is the Argonaut herald, son of Hermes and Eupolemeia daughter of Myrmidon of Phthia, born near the Amphrysus. Hermes granted him unfailing memory even in Hades and alternating sojourn above and below; later tradition makes his soul migrate through Euphorbus, Hermotimus, Pyrrhus, and Pythagoras.

sections.heading: Herald of the Argo
paragraphs: Apollonius makes Aethalides son of Hermes and Eupolemeia, sailing with his paternal half-brothers Erytus and Echion. He is the unfailing herald of the host: his father gave him the faculty of remembering everything, even after death, and leave to dwell alternately in the upper and lower worlds.

Diogenes Laërtius preserves the Pythagorean strand in which the same remembering soul passes from Aethalides into Euphorbus, Hermotimus, Pyrrhus, and finally Pythagoras — still recalling its former lives. Hyginus and the Orphic Argonautica include him among the crew.

sections.heading: Homonym note
paragraphs: Aethalides is this Argonaut herald alone in the atlas; he is not a Trojan or local namesake outside the Jason tradition.
